target:
inductive Form : Type
  | atom (r x y : ℕ) : Form
  | fls : Form
  | imp (φ ψ : Form) : Form
  | all (x : ℕ) (φ : Form) : Form
  | K (φ : Form) : Form

def neg (φ : Form) : Form := imp φ fls

def and (φ ψ : Form) : Form := neg (imp φ (neg ψ))

def iff (φ ψ : Form) : Form := and (imp φ ψ) (imp ψ φ)

def ex (x : ℕ) (φ : Form) : Form := neg (all x (neg φ))

def Def6 (x : ℕ) : Form → Prop
  | atom _ a b => x = a ∨ x = b
  | fls => False
  | imp φ ψ => Def6 x φ ∨ Def6 x ψ
  | all y φ => x ≠ y ∧ Def6 x φ
  | K φ => Def6 x φ

def Def7 (x y : ℕ) : Form → Form
  | atom r a b => atom r (if a = x then y else a) (if b = x then y else b)
  | fls => fls
  | imp φ ψ => imp (Def7 x y φ) (Def7 x y ψ)
  | all z φ => if z = x then all z φ else all z (Def7 x y φ)
  | K φ => K (Def7 x y φ)

def Def8 (y x : ℕ) : Form → Prop
  | atom _ _ _ => True
  | fls => True
  | imp φ ψ => Def8 y x φ ∧ Def8 y x ψ
  | all z φ => z = x ∨ ¬ Def6 x φ ∨ (z ≠ y ∧ Def8 y x φ)
  | K φ => Def8 y x φ

divergences.description: Relative to Reinhardt's source passages (which use the language of arithmetic with constants, function symbols, equality, and term substitution p(x/t)), the Lean language restricts atomic formulas strictly to binary relation symbols over variables, with no function symbols, constants, equality, or arithmetic, and correspondingly restricts substitution (Def7) and substitutability (Def8) to variables rather than arbitrary terms. This fragment restriction is explicitly noted in the author's claim as declared separately.

judgement.summary: The Lean definitions accurately implement the claimed relational fragment extended with the operator K, the standard classical connectives (neg, and, iff, ex), and the standard syntactic notions of free variable occurrence (Def6), variable-for-variable substitution (Def7, recursing inside K), and substitutability/free-for (Def8, recursing inside K). The only divergence from the source passages is the explicitly acknowledged restriction from Reinhardt's language of arithmetic and general term substitution to a purely binary relational language with variable-only substitution.
